chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the Hajj obligatory upon the inhabitants of Al-Jeddah every year.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Hajj for the inhabitants of Jeddah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'Takhyir' (choice) in Hajj obligations, where Allah grants ease to those with the capacity ('Ahl al-Jiddah') to perform it annually. While the majority of Shia scholars interpret 'Jiddah' as general financial and physical ability applicable to all Muslims, this narration is often cited to support the view that Hajj is not strictly limited to once in a lifetime for those who can afford it repeatedly. The mention of 'Ahl al-Jiddah' underscores the divine mercy in accommodating the logistical ease of certain communities, such as the people of Jeddah, who historically had convenient access to the Holy Sanctuary.
